newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Tungsten to sell tungsten assets.
newsitem.headline: Canada Tungsten to sell tungsten assets.

text.p: Canada Tungsten Inc wants to sell off its tungsten assets, a company spokesman said on Wednesday.
"We plan to sell them," company secretary Peter McCarter told Reuters.
He said the tungsten market has been not performed well recently and company management is pessimistic about the future of the market.
Canada Tungsten has been negotiating with "interested parties," he said, but he would not name them.

The company's current tungsten assets include the Cantung property in the Northwest Territories, which has been shut since 1986 because of low prices. It also holds the undeveloped Mactung property on the Yukon-Northwest Territories border.
Canada Tungsten holds a 100 percent interest in the Hemerdon tungsten-tin deposit near Plymouth, England.
It also receives a net profit interest from an ammonium metatungstate processing operationg near Bishop, California.
The company's main asset is the Andacollo copper project in Chile.

Aur Resources Inc already owns 46 percent of Canada Tungsten, but wants to increase its holdings to 100 percent and has proposed a merger, which Canada Tungsten shareholders will consider for approval on Monday.
Advisers to an independent committee have recommended Canada Tungsten shareholders vote in favor of the offer.

Canada Tungsten shareholders will get one common share and one common share purchase warrant for each 4.5 common shares of Canada Tungsten. Each Aur warrant will permit the holder to buy one common share of Aur for C$9.50 on or prior to June 30, 1997.
Tungsten is a strong, brittle metal used in drill bits, light bulbs, aerospace and military applications.
